newsitem.title: USA: ITT Educational plans to open new colleges.
newsitem.headline: ITT Educational plans to open new colleges.

text.p: ITT Educational Services Inc, a private college system focused on technology-oriented programs of study, said Wednesday it will open new colleges and add to its programs of study in 1997.

"We will continue to pursue growth on a number of fronts, including expansion of our college base, with plans to start a new college in 1997 in Las Vegas, St. Louis, Chicago and Northern California," said Rene Champagne, chairman and president. "The addition of curricula in existing colleges at both the associate's and bachelor's degree levels are also a top priority," he said in a statement.
ITT Educational operates 59 ITT Technical Institutes in 26 states which provide career-focused degree programs.
ITT Educational reported its 1996 year-end earnings rose 31 percent from a year ago to $14.9 million or $0.55 a share. Revenues in 1996 rose 15 percent to $232.3 million.

The company attributed its strong earnings growth to a 10 percent increase in student enrollment for the year. This was due to an increase in same-college student enrollments, the maturation of new colleges opened over the last three years, expanded curricula offerings and the introduction of new baccalaureate programs, it said.

As of December 31, 1996, total student enrollment increased 10 percent to 22,633, compared with 20,618 at the end of 1995. Same-college new student enrollments increased 13 percent to 21,040 students for the year ended December 31, 1996, compared with 18,645 students for the year ended December 31, 1995.
The gains reflect a growing demand for technology-oriented postsecondary programs, ITT Educational said in a statement.
Champagne also said, that "Based on current trends, we are optimistic about maintaining our long-term growth rate in net earnings for the coming year.

"Most encouraging is that even with ongoing investments in new colleges and curricula, our financial condition continues to strengthen, with over $95 million in cash and equivalents at the end of December 1996," he said.
ITT Educational shares were trading unchanged at 26-1/4.
